name: Session 1 - The World Of Data
summary:
{%:Introduction}In order to successfully grow a business, one must plan carefully. What is more, in today’s digital world business decision makers need direct access to real time, reliable, relevant and actionable data in order to make critical business decisions every day. Data helps us to understand the area the business is in, its main competitors, its market niche, its customers, its strategies, its risks, how experience the management team, return on investment, return on equity and so on. In summary, the best way to predict the future is to create it.

{%} {%:Guidelines}

Prior to session one, complete all required readings and review the materials contained in the pre-workshop section of LMS.

{%} {%:Learning Outcomes}

By the end of this session you will be able to:

-       Review the unit scope.

-       Develop an understanding of the unit assessment requirements.

-       Begin to understand how to create value for business with data analytics.

-       Gain an understanding of how we could use data for decision-making.

{%} {%:Resources}

To undertake study for this topic, it is recommended that you read the Learning Module (Topic 1 (see LMS)).

{%}

name: Session 2 - Data Analytics for Business
summary:
{%:Introduction}

Data analytics (DA) is the process of examining data sets to draw conclusions about the information they contain, increasingly with the aid of specialized systems and software. Data analytics is widely used in business to enable organizations make better business decisions and by scientists and researchers to verify or disprove scientific hypotheses. First step in DA is to gather the data that we want to analyse.

{%}{%:Guidelines}

Prior to session two, complete all required readings and review the materials contained in the pre-workshop section of LMS.

{%} {%:Learning Outcomes}

-       Develop an understanding on Data Analytics and it’s relevance to business strategy planning and decision-making.

-       Develop ability to collect required data to help to drive business planning and strategy.

-       Consider the characteristics of a successful questionnaire. 

{%} {%:Resources}

To undertake study for this topic, it is recommended that you read the Learning Module (Topic 2 (see LMS)).

{%}

name: Session 3 - Analysing the Business Environment
summary:
{%:Introduction}

Broad environmental factors impact upon all businesses. Inflation, global warming, political unrest and demographic shifts in a local community influence economies, businesses and the way we live our lives.

The challenge for businesses seeking to make sense of what is often a very long and detailed list of ‘macro’ and often ‘micro’ local environmental factors is identifying which of these is most profoundly shaping success or failure in the present and which will shape success or failure in the future. 

{%} {%:Guidelines}

Prior to session three, complete all required readings and review the materials contained in the pre-workshop section of LMS.

{%} {%:Learning Outcomes}

-       Review the macro drivers of environmental change.

-       Explore the scenario planning process and consider how this can impact upon key business decisions. 

{%} {%:Resources}

To undertake study for this topic, it is recommended that you read the Learning Module (Topic 3 (see LMS)).

{%}

name: Session 4 - Analysing the Business Itself
summary:
{%:Introduction}

The main purpose of analysing the firm is to pinpoint its resources and investigate whether these are effectively utilised in building competitive advantage. This is an important step in establishing a company’s core competencies and thus aligning it towards these activities. Upon establishing its core competencies, the firm should then move to establish its core activities. Through this analysis, the firm is able to identify those activities within the value chain that the business is the strongest. 

{%} {%:Guidelines}

Prior to session four, complete all required readings and review the materials contained in the pre-workshop section of LMS.

{%} {%:Learning Outcomes}

-       Explore the firm’s resources and how these can be used to achieve a competitive advantage.

-       Evaluate the core competencies of a firm. 

{%} {%:Resources}

To undertake study for this topic, it is recommended that you read the Learning Module (Topic 4 (see LMS)).

{%}

name: Session 5 - Analysing The Industry
summary:
{%:Introduction}

When working in business, one must have a good understanding of the industry in which the firm is involved in as well as a sound knowledge of its competitors. To do this, several key questions should be asked and then carefully answered:

1. What is the current size and what are the major trends in the industry?
2. What are the main competitive forces?
3. Who are the firm’s competitors and what are their relative strengths?
4. How should the firm’s strategy be adapted to respond to industry changes? 

{%} {%:Guidelines}

Prior to session five, complete all required readings and review the materials contained in the pre-workshop section of LMS.

{%} {%:Learning Outcomes}

-       Review the macro/ micro drivers of industry change.

-       Explore the competitive environment and the competitors in an industry.

-       An assessment of change. 

{%} {%:Resources}

To undertake study for this topic, it is recommended that you read the Learning Module (Topic 5 (see LMS)).

{%}

name: Session 7 - Analytics for Decision Making (Heuristics)
summary:
{%:Introduction} Analytics help to discover and communicate meaningful patterns in data. If done well, it also enables us to make informed decisions. This is especially important when working in an organisation or planning to grow one's business. Today we will start looking at how we could employ data in the decision making process.

 

{%}{%:Guidelines}

Prior to session seven, complete all required readings and review the materials contained in the pre-workshop section of LMS.

 

{%}{%:Learning Outcomes}

-       Examine the basics of decision making.

-       Investigate how framing and heuristics could be used in the organisation.

 

{%} {%:Resources}

To undertake study for this topic, it is recommended that you read the Learning Module (Topic 7 (see LMS)).

 

{%}

name: Session 8 - Analytics for Decision Making (Marketing)
summary:
{%:Introduction} A vital component of any organisations strategy is marketing. The overall objective of a marketing strategy is to enable a company to position its products and services in a given market, based on an understanding of customer needs, attitudes and behaviours. In a competitive 21st century, it is extremely important to use data to make the right decisions in marketing and subsequently to be able to grow one's business successfully. 

 

{%}{%:Guidelines}

Prior to session eight, complete all required readings and review the materials contained in the pre-workshop section of LMS.

 

{%}{%:Learning Outcomes}

-       Review and assess consumer's decision making journey.

-       Examine an organisation could use data for marketing purposes. 

 

{%} {%:Resources}

To undertake study for this topic, it is recommended that you read the Learning Module (Topic 8 (see LMS)).

name: Session 9 - Analytics for Decision Making (Sentiment Analysis)
summary:
{%:Introduction} In the age of technology, businesses worldwide are presented with numerous opportunities to create better products for consumers and to increase their market share. One example of the use of technology for business purposes is Sentiment Analysis.

Sentiment analysis is the automated process of understanding an opinion about a given subject from written or spoken language. In a world where we generate 2.5 quintillion bytes of data every day, sentiment analysis has become a key tool for making sense of that data. This has allowed companies to get key insights and automate all kind of processes.

 

{%}{%:Guidelines}

Prior to session nine, complete all required readings and review the materials contained in the pre-workshop section of LMS.

 

{%}{%:Learning Outcomes}

-      Examine how sentiment analysis could be used by an organisation.  

-      Assess the role of sentiment analysis in decision making process.

 

{%} {%:Resources}

To undertake study for this topic, it is recommended that you read the Learning Module (Topic 9 (see LMS)).

 

{%}

name: Session 10 - Storytelling with Data I
summary:
{%:Introduction} Data is important. However even more vital is the ability to tell a story with it. Presenting the data the right way, allows one to keep the audience's attention, help stakeholders of the business to understand the data and make decisions. There are a number of tools that could help to create a compelling story using data. 

 

{%}{%:Guidelines}

Prior to session ten, complete all required readings and review the materials contained in the pre-workshop section of LMS.

 

{%}{%:Learning Outcomes}

-       Create a meaningful story using data.

-       Develop ability to show the data in a compelling way.

 

{%} {%:Resources}

To undertake study for this topic, it is recommended that you read the Learning Module (Topic 10 (see LMS)).

name: Session 11 - Storytelling with Data II
summary:
{%:Introduction}

Data is important. However even more vital is the ability to tell a story with it. Today's focus is data visualization - placing data in a visual context. Patterns, trends and correlations that might go undetected in big numeric or language datasets can be exposed and recognized easier with data visualization tools.

{%}{%:Guidelines}

Prior to session eleven, complete all required readings and review the materials contained in the pre-workshop section of LMS.

 

{%}{%:Learning Outcomes}

-       Visualize data using data visualisation tool.

-       Identify methods to present data using data visualisation.

 

{%} {%:Resources}

To undertake study for this topic, it is recommended that you read the Learning Module (Topic 11 (see LMS)).
